mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of rising unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real estate sales (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which boosts related industries and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increasing housing sales compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a weakening supply side, leading to reduced corporate output and earnings, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining industrial production compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter, it signals strong economic demand, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong GDP growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates high inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of high inflation and tight monetary policy compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% within a month, it signals a strengthening labor market, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong labor market improvement compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining retail sales compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
